sources.revenue_2026: FY2026 revenue, gross and recognized: base $55.8B, bear $50.0B, bull $60.0B. H1 is actual: Q1 $4.73B plus Q2 $11.5B = $16.23B (Bloomberg, Aug 14, from investor documents; Fortune's snapshot of the leaked draft prospectus lists the same figures; T2/T3, no public S-1; evt-20260929-q1-2026-rev-4-73b-q2-11-5b-prospectus, evt-20260814-q2-2026-rev-11-5b-first-report). H2 is built from the last verified run-rate, more than $65B at Jul 31 (Bloomberg via TechCrunch, T2; evt-20260817-rr-65b-end-july), with monthly revenue = average run-rate / 12. Q2 actual implies an end-June run-rate of $60.6B. Base adds $7B a month to $100B at Dec 31 (Q3 $17.2B, Q4 $22.4B). Bear adds $1.4B a month to $72B (Q3 $16.3B, Q4 $17.5B). Bull adds $11B a month to $120B (Q3 $17.9B, Q4 $25.9B). Year-end $100-120B run-rates are investor projections (T3), not actuals. PitchBook TTM 4Q2026 ($65B) and 4Q2027 ($71B) are forward fields and are not used. The desk-derived $64-72B needs Q3 of $20-23B, an average Q3 run-rate of $80-92B against $65B at Jul 31, so it is not used.
sources.growth: Growth applies to the prior year's recognized revenue. Base 2027-2030: +129%, +53%, +37%, +22.5%, which puts FY2028 at $195.5B inside Reuters' roughly $190-200B company projection (T2, Aug 17, basis not stated; evt-20260817-reuters-2028-190-200b-forecast). That plan was $70B in Nov 2025 (T3) and the company has under-forecast each time (FY2025 plan $2.2B vs $4.59B actual; FY2026 plan $18B vs $55.8B base), so the plan is an anchor, not a ceiling. Base growth decays by 0.41x, 0.70x, 0.61x a year after 2027; Nvidia data center decayed 0.65x then 0.48x. Implied exit run-rates: about $160B at Dec 2027 and $235B at Dec 2028, which at about $21B per GW (T4 blog; capacity not company-stated) is about 11 GW against 15.8 GW announced, 13.0 GW of it 'up to'. Bear: +59%, +20%, +17%, +14% (run-rate plateaus near $72B into 2027, then deflation and share loss cap growth). Bull: +165%, +62%, +38%, +26% (capacity fully used; FY2030 $448B, the top of PitchBook's $345-450B valuation-implied range, T3). FT's roughly $360B run-rate at end-2027 (T3, LOW) would put 2028 revenue at $360B or more even with no further growth, about 1.8x the company plan, and is not used.
sources.equalization: Default 0.3975 in all three scenarios (desk canonical, Jul 16); equalization_alt carries 0.076 (platform fees $351M = 7.6% of FY2025 revenue, Reuters leak, T3; evt-20260929-reuters-47pct-cloud-channel-mix) and PitchBook's 6-10% (T3; evt-20260916-pitchbook-s1-preview-gross-vs-net). The canonical figure is contradicted in size by the record: at 39.75% Q2 2026 would imply $4.6B paid to cloud partners in one quarter, against The Information's $1.9B forecast for all of 2026 (T3; evt-20260217-information-80b-cloud-spend-through-2029) and $351M in FY2025. It is also a fitted parameter: 1 - (965/47)/(852/25) = 0.3975, the haircut that ties Anthropic's $965B over $47B gross run-rate to OpenAI's $852B over $25B at 34.1x. It cannot be used as evidence that the two multiples are equal. Base EV / FY2026 net revenue at Series H, secondary, IPO target: 28.7x, 44.6x, 59.5x at 39.75%; 18.7x, 29.1x, 38.8x at 7.6%. EV / FY2027 net revenue: 12.5x, 19.5x, 26.0x at 39.75%; 8.2x, 12.7x, 16.9x at 7.6%. The haircut moves the net-basis rows and the EV/net multiples only; it does not move the DCF.
sources.gross_margin: Gross margin = 1 - inference cost of revenue. Cloud-partner share is booked in marketing expense (prospectus), so it sits in S&M, not here. FY2024 -94% (paying customers only; The Information, T3). FY2025 40% (The Information Jan 21, T3; 38% with free-user inference per PitchBook footnote). Q1 2026 about 29% and Q2 2026 about 44% are PitchBook compute-cost ratios (T3, definitions not stated). Company targets: 63% in 2027 (PitchBook compilation, VERIFY) and 77% in 2028 (The Information, T3); company-adjusted above 80% before partner share and training (FT, T3). No GAAP margin is reported. Base 48%, 57%, 64%, 68%, 70%: 6 pts below the 2027 target and 13 pts below the 2028 target, because the company already missed its FY2025 plan by 10 pts (inference cost 23% above plan) and margins persist (r = 0.72 over five years, Base Rate Book). The reason to move up is unit cost: about $8B per GW-year on TPU capacity vs $12-16B on rented Nvidia capacity (contract value / term / GW, desk arithmetic, 'up to' caveats). Bear 45%, 42%, 46%, 52%, 58%: take-or-pay cost on idle capacity plus price war. Bull 52%, 65%, 75%, 79%, 80%: plan met and the above-80% adjusted margin realized.
sources.inference_share: 0.92, an assumption (display split only; it does not move FCF). No cost-of-revenue breakdown is disclosed. PitchBook's 44% subtracts compute only, so compute is treated as the bulk of cost of revenue; the other 8% stands for support, payment processing and non-inference hosting. FY2025 paying-user inference was $2.75B at a 40% margin; free-user inference adds about 2 pts (T3/T4).
sources.opex: Opex excludes training compute. FY2025 non-compute cost is an identity from the leaked prospectus: total operating expenses $12.65B less compute and infrastructure $7.33B = $5.32B, 116% of revenue (T2; evt-20260928-reuters-draft-prospectus-2025-financials). FY2024: $3.37B less $2.44B = $0.93B. The split into R&D, S&M, G&A and SBC is not disclosed and is my assumption. Base S&M includes cloud-partner fees: 16 cents per marketplace dollar x 47% share = about 7.5-7.6% of FY2025 revenue ($351M; Reuters, T3); The Information forecast payouts of $1.9B for 2026 and $6.4B for 2027 (T3), 10.6% and 11.6% of the $18B and $55B plan revenues (desk arithmetic), so S&M is 13.0-13.5% through 2027, then 12.0%. R&D ex-training falls from 6.5% to 3.5% and G&A from 3.5% to 1.6% as revenue outgrows headcount (about 2,300 at Dec 2025, T2). SBC falls from 5.0% to 2.8%. Total opex including SBC: 27.0% of revenue in 2026, 19.9% in 2030. The $1.5B Bartz settlement (evt-20250905-bartz-1-5b-settlement) may sit in FY2025 G&A; no opened source itemizes it.
sources.training: Training compute, $B: base 13.0, 25.0, 35.0, 42.0, 48.0 for 2026-2030. FY2025 $4.58B = compute and infrastructure $7.33B (T2) less inference cost of revenue $2.75B at a 40% margin; FY2024 $1.69B = $2.44B (implied) less $0.75B. Forward anchors: $12B for 2026 (The Information, T3), then PitchBook's more than $12B, about $23B and about $30B for 2026-2028 (T3), set when revenue plans were $18B, $55B and $70B. Base keeps dollars near plan and lets the share of revenue fall from 23% to 15%. Cross-check: Anthropic's own report says one frontier model needs a 2 GW site in 2027 and 5 GW in 2028 (T1; evt-20250721-build-ai-in-america); at an assumed $9B per GW-year, base training is 2.8 GW-years in 2027 and 3.9 in 2028. Bear holds $17-18B (cut, not stopped). Bull is $30B, $45B, $55B, $65B for 2027-2030.
sources.capex: Compute capex and prepayments outside cost of revenue and training. The record has no capex or prepayment figure; the S-1 cash-flow statement is not public. Most compute is leased or hosted, so its cost sits in cost of revenue or training: the $34.5B TPU notes are lessor debt, Fluidstack, TeraWulf and Riot are leases, and the draft prospectus describes a shift toward dedicated data centers and directly leased chips (T2). The one owned item seen is a 470 MW onsite-power equipment order with no stated value (ERock, T1). Base: $2B in 2026 rising to $8B in 2030, 2.4-3.6% of revenue. Bear keeps $7B a year in 2027-2028 because about 80% of the $518B of commitments is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2; evt-20260929-compute-commitments-518b-80pct-non-cancelable). Bull: $3B rising to $19B as more capacity is owned. Tripling base capex cuts base DCF EV by 18%. This is the least-sourced cash line in the model.
sources.terminal: The terminal multiple applies to 2030 FCF; the engine adds the 2030 FCF itself. Base 20x, bear 15x, bull 26x, with a 12% discount rate in all three. Calibration: an explicit ten-year fade of FCF growth (22%, 18%, 14%, 11%, 8%, 6%, 4%, 3%, 3%, 3%) at 12% implies 19x; a bear-like fade implies 16x and a bull-like fade 25x. No company or peer multiple is in the record. DCF EV at 15x / 20x / 30x: base $924B / $1,189B / $1,717B; bear $176B / $233B / $347B; bull $1,623B / $2,083B / $3,004B. IPO absorption is the swing driver here: a reported raise of up to $100B (WSJ, T3) or at least $130B (The Information, T4) compares with SpaceX's $75B base and $85.7B with greenshoe, the largest IPO on record, and SK Hynix's $26.5B, the second largest. Bear assumes the raise does not clear near $2T and the market pays 15x FCF; bull assumes it clears and holds 26x.

outside_view.what_is_different: Growth: FY2025 was +1,088% and base FY2026 is +1,116%, about 5x the best year of any reference above $15B (Nvidia data center +217%). The run-rate went from $9B to $65B in seven months (7.2x); Nvidia data center's best year was 2.4x in twelve. Base regresses hard (2027 +129%, 2028 +53%, 2029 +37%, 2030 +22.5%, decay 0.41x, 0.70x, 0.61x) but its 2026-2030 CAGR of 56% sits in the top bin (45%+), which 0.0% of firms above $25B reached over five years. It needs compute that is contracted, not demanded: about 11 GW by Dec 2028 against 15.8 GW announced. Margins: FY2025 gross margin was 40% against 71-75% at Nvidia; AWS operating margin took six years to gain 9 pts. Base adds 30 pts of gross margin in five years, 13 pts below the company's 2028 target of 77%, on unit-cost declines, not on precedent. Capital: FY2025 compute was $7.33B, 1.6x revenue; commitments of at least $518B are 113x FY2025 revenue and 9.3x base FY2026 revenue, about 80% non-cancelable. Concentration and basis: 47% of FY2025 sales sits in cloud marketplaces that keep about 16 cents per dollar, two customers were about 24% of revenue, and revenue is gross while OpenAI's is net.

scenario_logic.bear: Share loss, faster deflation and compute overbuild together. Coding and agents are the swing: SpaceX agreed to buy Cursor for $60B (T1), OpenAI priced Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 (T3), and Claude Code and agents fall to 16% of 2030 revenue (base 24%). List prices keep falling about 40% a year (Opus -73% in 14 months) and volume does not outrun it, so the run-rate plateaus near $72B into 2027 and revenue grows +59%, +20%, +17%, +14%. About 80% of the $518B of commitments is non-cancelable, so compute cost holds near $63-72B a year while revenue is $80-127B: gross margin 42% in 2027, cumulative FCF trough -$25.9B in 2028, FCF positive in 2029. The IPO does not clear near $2T and the market pays 15x FCF. DCF EV $176B.
scenario_logic.base: Capacity-gated growth to the company plan. Revenue follows the T2 projection (FY2028 $195.5B against $190-200B) because the prospectus says demand is limited by compute; contracted capacity arrives roughly on schedule (base needs about 11 GW by Dec 2028 against 15.8 GW announced). Price deflation is offset by volume and by a shift to agents. Gross margin climbs to 64% in 2028 (plan 77%), training rises to $35B, cloud partners keep 10-12% of revenue, and FCF turns positive in 2027 ($13.7B) and reaches 28.4% of revenue in 2030. The IPO clears and the market pays 20x FCF. DCF EV $1,189B.
scenario_logic.bull: Agents and capacity at full utilization. The year-end 2026 run-rate reaches $120B (the FT figure), the 15.8 GW of announced capacity is used in full, and revenue per dollar of compute is about 29% above base as work moves to agents and to frontier tiers priced at $10/$50. Claude Code and agents reach 31% of 2030 revenue. The company meets its own margin targets (65% in 2027, 75% in 2028) and the above-80% adjusted margin becomes a reported one by 2030. FY2030 revenue is $448B, FCF margin 36.2%, compute spend $155B. The raise of $100B or more is absorbed and the market holds 26x FCF. DCF EV $2,635B.
